result.summary: The environment is a high-capacity arterial road with multiple travel lanes and a lack of visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure at the signalized intersection. The design prioritizes vehicle throughput, resulting in long crossing distances and high exposure for anyone attempting to cross on foot.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least six lanes of traffic without a marked crosswalk or refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The signalized intersection lacks visible pedestrian signal heads, leaving pedestrians without a dedicated crossing phase.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection corners and overhead signal mast arms

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight lanes and large turning radii encourage high vehicle speeds through the intersection.

interventions.title: Marked High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings on all legs of the intersection to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Construct raised islands in the center of the roadway to reduce exposure and allow for two-stage crossings.

result.summary: The intersection features wide roadways with significant crossing distances and large turning radii that favor vehicle speed. While a marked crosswalk and sidewalks are present on one side, the environment is dominated by heavy vehicle traffic and lacks comprehensive pedestrian protection across all legs.

hazards.name: Large Turning Radius
hazards.description: The wide corner geometry allows vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.
